Every fleet must define every capability key. A fleet missing a key would
emit an empty runs-on, and an empty or unknown label does not error on
GitHub: the job sits queued forever and holds its concurrency group. The
resolver refuses to start on a fleet with a missing key for that reason.
Capability keys are requirements, not lanes. Who is asking (pull request,
manual flake hunt, non-urgent background work) is cost policy and is not

capabilities.linux: x86_64 Linux; the default for every non-macOS job
capabilities.linux_16: x86_64 Linux, 16 vCPU: CPU-bound jobs (compiles, linters, large test suites)
capabilities.linux_32: x86_64 Linux, 32 vCPU: the largest parallel builds and test shards
capabilities.linux_arm64: aarch64 Linux; native ARM64 package entrypoint verification
capabilities.macos_15: macOS 15 image, and therefore the macOS 15 default SDK
capabilities.macos_15_gui: macOS 15 with a foreground Aqua login session (XCUITest, virtual display)
capabilities.macos_15_sdk15: macOS 15 carrying an SDK 15 Xcode alongside the pinned one
capabilities.macos_26_ios: macOS 26 with installed iOS runtimes and a working simctl
capabilities.macos_26_large: macOS 26 on the large SKU: 12 vCPU, 48 GB RAM, 250 GB disk

apple-app-build.description: Builds the macOS app, an Apple framework or an xcframework with Xcode or SwiftPM against AppKit, SwiftUI or WebKit, or seeds those builds' caches.

apple-swift-tests.description: Swift tests of packages that import Darwin, Foundation networking, CryptoKit, Security, AppKit or another Apple-only framework.

apple-gui.description: Needs a macOS login session or window server: UI tests, app-host tests, captures, tours, frame benchmarks.

apple-ios.description: iOS builds, simulators and App Store Connect tooling.

apple-signing-release.description: Signs, notarizes, staples, verifies or publishes Apple release artifacts with codesign, notarytool or the keychain.

macos-runtime-tests.description: Tests how code behaves on macOS itself: PTYs, launchd, the system keychain, the network stack, an Intel run-time check, a built binary launched on macOS.

rust-darwin-release-build.description: Release builds of the Rust macOS targets that link against the real Apple SDK and package npm and PyPI. Compile-only checks of those targets are rust-darwin-compile.

rust-darwin-compile.description: Compiles the Rust macOS targets without running them; scripts/ci/macos-cross.sh does this on Linux (darwin_builder: linux).

cpp-unit-tests.description: Compiles and runs C or C++ unit tests that use only the standard library; clang++ on Linux runs them.

shell-parse.description: Parses or lints shell scripts, including with a specific bash version, which can be built on Linux.

portable-swift-packages.description: Swift packages that build without Apple-only frameworks; swift test runs them on Linux.

web-and-tooling.description: TypeScript, JavaScript, Python or Rust tests, linters, formatters and generators that do not call Apple tools.
